title: Developing A Maqasid-Based Governance Framework for Islamic Banking: Integrating Ethics, Sustainability, and Digital Transformation
summary: This study conceptualizes a Maqasid-Based Governance Framework (MBGF) for Islamic banking in Indonesia. Using a qualitative-conceptual approach, the study synthesizes maqāṣid al-sharīʿah, Value-Based Intermediation (VBI), Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG), and digital ethics. The conceptual analysis indicates that compliance-based governance has not yet comprehensively connected Shariah objectives with institutional mechanisms and outcome-based accountability. MBGF comprises four interrelated components: maqāṣid ethical foundations, institutional governance through VBI, sustainability through ESG, and digital-ethics safeguards. Maqāṣid functions as the normative criterion, institutional governance translates it into organizational practices, while ESG and digital ethics operate as parallel domains of application. The framework is a conceptual proposition rather than an empirically validated causal model. Its contribution lies in integrating previously fragmented governance perspectives and providing a foundation for expert validation, indicator development, and further empirical testing.

title: Digital Economy and Taxation of Crypto Assets: A Model Proposal for Turkey
summary: This study examines the taxation problems of crypto assets in Turkey, which have increased in importance with the development of the digital economy and aims to reveal the gaps in the legal definition and integration of these assets into the tax system. The main objective of the study is to identify the shortcomings and implementation problems in the current legislation and to propose an effective and applicable crypto asset taxation model specific to Turkey in the light of international examples. The qualitative method was adopted in the study; national legislation, regulatory body reports, academic studies and policies of international organizations (OECD, IMF, etc.) were examined using document review and content analysis techniques. The findings show that although Turkey ranks high in the world rankings in the use of crypto assets, legal and tax regulations in this area are inadequate. As a result, the study recommends the legal definition of crypto assets as “digital assets”, the creation of a new income category under the title of “digital asset income”, exemptions for individual investors and the development of platform-based audit mechanisms.

title: Effect of Accounting Conservatism on Firm Value of Non-Financial Firms Listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange
summary: This paper examined the effect of accounting conservatism on firm value among non-financial firms listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange. The study was anchored in Signaling Theory and adopted a positivist philosophy and an explanatory longitudinal design. The target population comprised 40 non-financial listed firms, of which 33 met the inclusion criteria for the period 2015-2024, yielding a balanced panel of 330 firm-year observations. Secondary data were obtained from audited annual reports, published financial statements, Capital Markets Authority records, and Nairobi Securities Exchange handbooks. Firm value was measured using approximate Tobin's Q, while conditional accounting conservatism was measured using the Basu asymmetric-timeliness model. Data were analyzed in STATA using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, diagnostic tests, panel unit-root tests, the Hausman specification test, and fixed-effects regression. Accounting conservatism was positively correlated with firm value (r = .277, p < .01). The fixed-effects model was statistically significant, F(6, 281) = 51.68, p < .001, and accounting conservatism had a positive and statistically significant effect on firm value after accounting for the other financial-reporting dimensions and firm controls (β = 0.880, SE = 0.278, t = 3.160, p = .002; 95% CI [0.332, 1.428]). The null hypothesis was therefore rejected. The study concludes that prudent recognition of losses and delayed recognition of uncertain gains enhance the credibility of financial statements and support higher market valuation. Firms should institutionalize consistent conservative reporting, strengthen audit oversight, and apply impairment, provision, and contingent-liability policies in line with applicable financial-reporting standards. Regulators should reinforce consistent compliance and disclosures without encouraging deliberate understatement that could obscure a firm's underlying economic performance. title: Assessing the Relationship Between Financial Reporting Quality and Investment Decision Making in Listed Consumer Goods Companies in Nigeria
summary: This research found that the quality of financial reports has a correlation with investment choices made by publicly listed Nigerian consumer goods businesses. Relevance, true representation, and comparability are three essential aspects of financial reporting quality that influence investors' judgments about portfolio selection and the efficiency of capital allocation. The purpose of this research is to respond to rising questions over the value and accuracy of financial statements. The research examined main data gathered from ninety-two investment professionals using methods such as multiple regression, correlation, and descriptive statistics. A descriptive and explanatory method was used in the investigation. Despite its small size and lack of statistical significance, the findings demonstrated a favorable correlation between investment decision-making and financial reporting quality. Among the expected traits, relevance had the smallest impact, while accuracy in depiction and comparability had the next to-smallest impacts. The regression model showed that the specific characteristics of financial reporting quality could only account for 6.5% of the variance in investment choices, with a R² value of 0.065. The F-statistic demonstrated that the model was not statistically significant at the 5% level (2.053, p > 0.05), even though the Durbin-Watson statistic did not indicate any autocorrelation at 1.93. Even if this were true in principle, the paper claims that investors' behavior, macroeconomic instability, and a lack of confidence in disclosures would prevent high-quality financial reporting from having a practical impact on the Nigerian consumer products market. By enhancing reporting timeliness and comparability, raising auditing standards, and providing comprehensive investor education, it aims to allow better use of financial data in capital markets.

title: Research on the Innovation of Enterprise Economic Management Models in the Digital Economy Era
summary: With the rapid expansion of the digital economy, enterprises face substantial changes in their operational environment and daily management. Conventional enterprise business management can no longer adapt to the current highly competitive market. This paper looks at how Chinese businesses change their management in the digital age. It describes new features of modern business management, points out three key weaknesses within older management systems, and searches for practical improvement methods. Adopting the literature research method, this study draws on Chinese journal articles, industry survey data, and public cases of enterprise digital transformation. It shows that old-fashioned management ideas, imperfect data systems and a shortage of digitally literate talent are the main barriers to business reform. Companies can address these practical problems by renewing management ideas, building shared data platforms, perfecting talent training and establishing robust data security policies.

title: From sensor data to supply chain decisions: a mechanism framework for IIoT and sensor networks in automotive supply chains
summary: Automotive logistics and supply chain networks coordinate complex multi-tier material flows under strict sequencing, transport synchronization, and quality constraints. These systems are highly sensitive to information-flow latency, exception-handling delays, and disruptions affecting inbound, production, and distribution logistics processes. Although Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and sensor-network technologies enable real-time visibility across material and transport flows, prior literature frequently emphasizes technological capability rather than clearly operationalized logistics decision mechanisms. This study develops a decision-centric mechanism framework explaining how IIoT-enabled sensing is translated into governed logistics decisions influencing reliability, responsiveness, inventory–production synchronization, and disruption mitigation in automotive supply chains. Based on a structured 2025 literature review (Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore; n = 13 included studies), four recurring sensor-to-decision mechanisms are identified: (M1) real-time visibility and traceability control, (M2) predictive asset and quality logistics, (M3) inventory–production flow synchronization, and (M4) event-driven logistics decision support. The contribution lies in formalizing reproducible sensor-to-decision pathways that connect sensing capability, analytics, decision triggers, and execution routines to measurable logistics performance outcomes.

title: Corporate Governance Practices and Performance in theFinancial Sector of Bangladesh: An Analysis betweenBanks and Non-Bank Financial Institutions
summary: This research study focuses on correlation between corporate governance practices and financial performance of banks and non-bank financial institutions (NBFIs) listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) in Bangladesh between 2014 and 2024. The paper applies the pooled OLS regression analysis on a total of 407 firm-years of 37 institutions (27 banks and 10 NBFIs) to analyze the impact of governance on the performance (ROA) based on accounting and (Tobin Q) based on the market. The results show that the size of the board and female diversity positively contribute to ROA, whereas independent directors have a negative impact on performance. The independence of audit committee has a negative correlation with ROA and a positive correlation with Q of Tobin which indicates a trade-off between ROA and confidence of investors. The size of the firm enhances ROA and decreases its market value whereas depreciation of currency has an adverse impact on profitability. These findings imply that, instead of paying lip service to the governance mechanisms, effective implementation is the key to enhancing the performance of the institutions.

title: Exploring the Influence of Corporate Social Responsibility on Organisational Performance in the Telecommunications Industry in Zimbabwe: A Case Study of Telone
summary: This study explores the relationship between Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives and the performance of TelOne, a top telecommunications company in Zimbabwe. The research investigates how TelOne's CSR efforts like economic, ethical, philanthropic and environmental responsibilities, influence the company's overall results in terms of financial performance, employee engagement and customer satisfaction. Qualitative research methods that include document findings and interviews were used to understand the problem. The study adopted the inductive approach to gather respondents‘ opinions about the impact of CSR on the performance of TelOne, resulting in deeper understanding of the problem understudy. The sample size was 20 respondents, obtained after purposively selecting 10 employees, five executives and five external stakeholders, based on convenience and personal judgement that they would provide credible information regarding how CSR influences the performance of TelOne. The results provide direction on the strategic importance of CSR in enhancing the performance of TelOne. This study theoretically contributes to the enhancement of knowledge on the connection between the concept of CSR and organisational performance. It practically contributes to the development of CSR strategies that enhance the performance of TelOne, including building internal capacity, looking into innovative finance options and investing and public-private partnerships.

title: Digital Technologies, Justice, Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Operations in Supply Chain Management: The Moderating Effect of Organizational Culture
summary: This study investigates how digital technologies shape justice, diversity, equity, and inclusion (JDEI) in operations and supply chain management (OSCM), with organizational culture as a moderator. Drawing on the newly proposed Digital Justice and Inclusion Theory (DJIT), we develop and test a structural model using survey data from 400 professionals in Nigerian quoted non-financial firms. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) results reveal that perceived ease of use is the strongest predictor of justice, diversity, and equity outcomes, while behavioral intention and perceived usefulness significantly enhance inclusion. Organizational culture strengthens the effects of digital technologies on justice, equity, and inclusion, but not diversity. The findings advance theory by integrating digital transformation and social sustainability literatures, challenging techno-determinist views, and contextualizing JDEI in an emerging-market setting. This study contributes to theory by integrating digital transformation and social justice paradigms and offers practical insights for building inclusive digital supply chains in emerging economies.

(2012) Oxford Handbook where no unified theory exists. Regulatory stringency moderates governance-performance interaction beta 0.12 stronger under mandatory EU CSRD 1,200 data points double materiality (Armour et al., 2023) versus voluntary SEC Climate Rule March 6 2024 stayed April 2024. ISO 37301 certified firms have 40% lower FCPA violations controlling for Federal Sentencing Guidelines seven elements (Laufer, 2006). US Dodd-Frank whistleblower bounty 10-30% $1.9bn awards generating 12,000 tips per year versus EU Directive 2019/1937 no bounty 1,200 tips per year (Silverman, 2020; Hopt & Voigt, 2022). Regulatory capture theory (Stigler, 1975; Carpenter & Moss, 2013) explains Boeing-FAA and predicts AI capture risk $100m lobbying. title: Environmental Responsibility and Financial Disclosure: A Green Accounting, CSR Model for Public Sector Tourism
summary: Background: Focusing on Manado, Indonesia, a coastal destination balancing growth and ecological risk, we develop and test an integrative model grounded in stakeholder and legitimacy theories that links environmental management accounting (EMA), CSR commitment, and environmental disclosure quality (EDQ). Objective: This study examines how green accounting and corporate social responsibility (CSR) jointly advance environmental responsibility and financial disclosure within public-sector tourism governance. Methods: An explanatory mixed-methods design was employed: survey data from tourism organizations were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and triangulated through expert interviews and focus group discussions with key stakeholders, including government agencies, hotels, and tour operators. Results: The results indicate that both EMA and CSR are significant, positive predictors of EDQ, with CSR exerting a marginally stronger effect. Certification status and enterprise type do not significantly moderate these relationships, implying that the EMA–CSR bundle improves transparency across heterogeneous tourism entities. Substantively, embedding EMA metrics into budgeting and decision-making processes, paired with CSR programs that engage communities and regulators, strengthens public financial disclosure and environmental accountability at the destination level. Conclusion: The study contributes a measurable framework for sustainable tourism governance in emerging regions and offers actionable guidance for policymakers to standardize indicators, require periodic disclosure, and pair certification with assurance and data-quality controls.

title: Corporate Governance Mechanism and Performance of Deposit Money Banks: A Theoretical Discourse

(2026).Corporate Governance Mechanism and Performance of Deposit Money Banks: A Theoretical Discourse.Afrisophia: Journal of African Experiment, Thought and Experience, Vol. 3, No. 3, pp. 1-23. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22673995 AbstractCorporate governance mechanisms constitute a fundamental pillar upon which the performance of deposit money banks rests, particularly in developing economies where regulatory frameworks and institutional environments present unique challenges to effective bank management. This paper examines the theoretical linkage between corporate governance mechanisms and bank performance, drawing extensively from agency theory, stewardship theory, and resource dependence theory to construct a comprehensive theoretical discourse on how governance structures shape financial outcomes in deposit money banks. The study explores key governance dimensions including board diversity, board independence, board supervision, and audit committee effectiveness, and their respective connections to bank performance measured through profitability, asset quality, and operational efficiency. The theoretical analysis reveals that robust governance structures significantly reduce agency conflicts between shareholders and management, align managerial incentives with organisational objectives, and facilitate access to critical resources that enhance competitive advantage. The paper further situates its arguments within the institutional context of deposit money banks in developing economies, where governance deficits have historically contributed to bank distress and financial instability. The study contributes to the existing theoretical corpus by synthesising competing perspectives on governance effectiveness and proposing contextualised theoretical propositions that advance scholarly understanding of the governance-performance nexus. The implications for regulatory policy, board structure design, and institutional reforms in the banking sector are carefully delineated, offering a robust platform for future empirical inquiry. title: Supply chain visibility and customer-oriented performance: mediation and moderation analysis of supply chain collaboration and learning
summary: Purpose Although supply chain management literature implicitly highlights supply chain visibility (SCV) as a customer-focused capability that can critically influence customer-oriented outcomes, there is a paucity of empirical research on the impact of SCV on customer-oriented outcomes. The paper examines the relationship between supply chain visibility (SCV) and customer-oriented performance (COP). Additionally, the paper examines the mediating and moderating roles of supply chain collaboration (SCC) and supply chain learning (SCL) in the relationship between SCV and COP. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional survey of manufacturing firms in Ghana was conducted, and 228 usable responses were received. The hypothesized paths were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings The results revealed that SCV has a positive and significant relationship with COP. The results also revealed that SCC significantly mediates the indirect relationship between SCV and COP. The results further revealed that SCL moderates the relationship between SCV and COP. Originality/value This study extends the SCV literature by broadening its performance outcomes to include COP and by explaining how and when SCV creates customer value. Specifically, it identifies SCC as the mechanism through which SCV enhances COP and demonstrates that SCL strengthens this relationship.

title: Board Gender Diversity and ESG Performance: A Systematic Literature Review and Meta‐Analysis
summary: ABSTRACT The relationship between board gender diversity (BGD) and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance remains inconclusive, yielding conflicting paradoxes and unresolved theoretical tensions. To address this theoretical and empirical vagueness, this study provides a comprehensive synthesis of the BGD and ESG performance nexus across aggregate and its pillar‐level dimensions. Utilizing a rigorous, dual‐methodological approach, following the PRISMA protocol, this research study analyzed 75 peer‐reviewed articles for systematic literature review (SLR) and 35 empirical studies for meta‐analysis, all retrieved from the Scopus database covering 2018 to 2025. The results confirm a robust positive association between BGD and aggregate ESG performance along with its pillars. Critically, the meta‐analysis reveals significant heterogeneity across the studies, which suggests that this relationship is contingent upon contextual and methodological preferences. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this research study is the first of its kind to investigate the impact of BGD on ESG performance by uniquely integrating meta‐analysis and SLR evidence. Ultimately, this study reconciles conflicting findings in corporate governance literature and reports that BGD functions as an effective corporate governance mechanism translating into quantifiable sustainability outcomes.

title: Digital Transformation of Teacher Education under Vikshit Bharat @2047
summary: Abstract India's vision of Vikshit Bharat @2047 rests on building a digitally empowered, innovation-driven, and sustainable economy in which artificial intelligence, e-commerce, and digital infrastructure serve as engines of inclusive growth. Realising this vision depends critically on the quality of human capital that education systems produce, and teacher education stands at the centre of that pipeline. This paper examines how the digital transformation envisaged under Vikshit Bharat @2047 is reshaping teacher education in India, using the reforms introduced under the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 as the entry point. It discusses how national digital platforms such as DIKSHA, SWAYAM, and PM eVIDYA, together with emerging technologies including artificial intelligence, virtual and augmented reality, blockchain, and the Internet of Things, are creating new possibilities for personalised, inclusive, and lifelong teacher development. The paper also situates these developments within the wider digital economy, arguing that a technologically competent teaching workforce is a precondition for the commerce, innovation, and productivity gains that Vikshit Bharat @2047 anticipates. At the same time, the paper identifies significant risks, including the digital divide, uneven digital literacy among teachers, and adverse effects of excessive technology use on mental well-being, sleep, and attention. Drawing on secondary literature and policy documents, the paper proposes a blended and sustainability-oriented framework for teacher education that combines digital tools with face-to-face mentoring, structured digital wellness training, and continuous monitoring of technology use. It concludes that India's digital future will be strongest where digital ambition is matched with digital responsibility, and where teacher education is treated as strategic national infrastructure rather than a peripheral concern.

title: 小尺寸双线性矩阵乘法算法的可验证加法清单与鸽笼下界
summary: Bilinear matrix-multiplication algorithms have a fifty-year record of multiplication counts, but their addition counts lack any accounting convention: rarely reported, never independently verified, and without a non-trivial lower bound. Under a unified cost convention this paper gives machine-verified addition inventories for three landmark formats: 3×3 rank-23 at 58 (an independent re-verification of Perminov's inventory, including full symbolic checking of the Brent equations), 4×4 rank-49 at 194, and 4×4 rank-48 (Dumas et al.) at 332 — the first complete accounting of that algorithm's addition cost, compressed from a naive count of 1,760 to 332. The tool is a scheme-agnostic optimization engine (global greedy overlapping common-subexpression elimination plus a Tellegen transposition module). We further prove a pigeonhole lower bound on the number of input linear forms: PLB(3,23) = 3 and PLB(4,48) = 7, and measure the remaining optimization headroom of a scheme by the CSE overhead δ. All inventories are accompanied by exact rational replay certificates. Series: Wuliang Method (WLM) paper series — Third Series "Bilinear Complexity Engineering" (P9). title: Do domestic and foreign institutional ownership shape the link between ESG disclosure and cost of debt? Evidence from the Indonesia Sharia Stock Index
summary: This study examines whether the association between environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure and firms’ cost of debt varies according to the origin of institutional ownership. The analysis focuses on non-financial firms in the Indonesia Sharia Stock Index (ISSI) over 2018–2023. This study analyzes a purposively selected unbalanced panel of 717 firm-year observations using moderated regression analysis in EViews 13. The findings show that greater ESG disclosure is associated with lower debt financing costs, indicating that creditors incorporate sustainability-related information into their assessment of firm risk. Domestic institutional ownership has no significant direct association with the cost of debt, while foreign institutional ownership is negatively associated with borrowing costs. The interaction between ESG disclosure and domestic institutional ownership is statistically insignificant, providing no evidence that domestic institutions alter the ESG–debt cost relationship. In contrast, the positive and significant interaction involving foreign institutional ownership indicates that foreign ownership changes the strength of the negative association between ESG disclosure and the cost of debt. These findings imply a substitution mechanism, in which the monitoring and informational advantages of foreign institutional investors may diminish the incremental value of ESG disclosure as a risk signal for creditors in an emerging Islamic capital market..

title: Financial Technology and Financial Reporting in the Public Sector: The Case of Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria
summary: Financial reporting in Nigeria’s public sector is often constrained by manual processes, bureaucratic inefficiencies, and error-prone procedures, leading to challenges in timely and accurate compliance with International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS). This study examined the relationship between financial technology and financial reporting compliance in the Akwa Ibom State public sector. A survey research design was adopted, with a population comprising all 58 staff members of the Offices of the Accountant-General and Auditor-General in Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria. Census sampling technique was employed, and data were collected using structured questionnaires on a 5-point Likert scale. Ordinary Least Squares regression was used for data analysis with SPSS 21. The instrument’s reliability was confirmed through Cronbach’s Alpha (0.771), while validity was ensured through supervisor evaluation and expert input. Findings revealed that the number of trained users, expenditure on financial software, and staff training hours on FinTech had significant positive relationships with financial reporting compliance, while revenue/expenditure automation platforms and telecoms/service provider partnerships showed no significant effect. The study concluded that financial technology significantly enhances compliance in public sector reporting. It recommended continuous staff training, investment in financial software, and improved integration of automation platforms to strengthen compliance and transparency in financial management.

title: Sustainable Leadership and Learning Organization Capacity in Schools: The Roles of Teachers’ Innovative Work Behavior and Corporate Social Responsibility in Türkiye
summary: This study examines the relationship between sustainable leadership and learning organization capacity in public schools, focusing on the behavioral and contextual roles of teachers’ innovative work behavior (IWB) and perceived corporate social responsibility (CSR). Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and social exchange theory, the study tests a moderated mediation model in which IWB is specified as a mediator of the relationship between sustainable leadership and learning organization capacity, while CSR is specified as a moderator of the relationship between sustainable leadership and IWB. Data were collected from 960 teachers working in public K–12 schools in Elazığ, Türkiye, and analyzed using structural equation modeling. The results showed that sustainable leadership was positively associated with both IWB and learning organization capacity, and the estimated indirect association through IWB was statistically significant. CSR moderated the sustainable leadership–IWB relationship, which was nonsignificant at low CSR but became significant at the mean level and stronger at high CSR. The conditional indirect effect through IWB showed a similar pattern, becoming significant at the mean level of CSR and increasing at higher levels. By integrating sustainable leadership, teacher innovation, and perceived school CSR, the study shows that the estimated indirect association between sustainable leadership and learning organization capacity through IWB varies across levels of perceived CSR.

title: Blockchain and IoT for Halal Supply-Chain Traceability: A Sharia-Compliance and Implementation Framework
summary: Halal integrity is a matter of trust in a chain that consumers cannot inspect. Certification, standards and audits exist to supply that trust, yet fraud, mislabelling and cross-contamination remain documented problems, and the supply chains that carry halal products are long, international and paper-heavy. Blockchain and the Internet of Things (IoT) are increasingly proposed as remedies, but the literature on them treats halal mainly as a product attribute to be tracked and pays little attention to what technology can and cannot decide under the Sharia. This paper proposes a Sharia-compliance and implementation framework for blockchain-and-IoT traceability in halal supply chains. Using an analytical synthesis of research on halal supply-chain management, halal standards, blockchain traceability, IoT sensing and technology adoption, it sets out compliance requirements, a four-layer architecture, rules on the division of labour between code and qualified human authorities, and a data-governance approach that limits on-chain data. A phased roadmap and pilot indicators are proposed for halal exporters, including smaller firms. The central argument is that technology can make the evidence for a halal claim harder to falsify, but it cannot determine halal status, and that the design must therefore keep certifiers and Sharia supervisors in charge of judgement. The framework is conceptual and has not been tested in a live supply chain.

title: DETECTING FRAUDULENT FINANCIAL REPORTING WITH FRAUD HEXAGON ANALYSIS
summary: Fraudulent financial reporting is a crucial issue that can undermine investor confidence and capital market stability. This study aims to analyze in depth the influence of the Fraud Hexagon elements on detecting fraudulent financial reporting. The six elements include: 1)pressure (stimulus), 2) opportunity, 3) rationalization, 4) capability, 5) arrogance, and 6) collusion. Financial Report Fraud (Y) is measured by F-Score = Accrual Quality + Financial Performances. While pressure (X1) is measured using financial stability (X1.1), external pressure (X1.2), and financial targets (X1.3). Opportunity (X2) is measured by ineffective monitoring (X2.1) and the nature of the industry (X2.2). Rationalization (X3) is measured using the total accrual ratio, Capability (X4) is measured by board of directors turnover, Arrogance (X5) is measured using the frequency of CEO photos, and Collusion (X6) is proxied through cooperation with the government. The study focused on infrastructure sector companies that went public during the period 2022 to 2024. The infrastructure sector was chosen because it is a large project that requires high investment, and is closely related to government projects. The study uses a quantitative approach with secondary data from the company's annual report. The sampling technique used purposive sampling, which resulted in a final sample of 35 companies over three years of observation, resulting in a total of 105 observation data. The data analysis technique used multiple linear regression analysis, with IBM SPSS to test the research hypothesis. The results of the Adjusted R Square value showed the influence of independent variables on the dependent variable in this study was 84.6%, while the remaining 15.4% was explained by other variables outside the research model. Variables X1.2 external pressure and X1.3 financial target, X2.2 nature of industry, X3 (Rationalization, measured by TATA), X4 (Ability, measured using change in director) and X5 (Arrogance, measured by CEO photo) were proven to have a positive effect on financial statement fraud. Conversely, X1 (Pressure, measured by financial stability), X2 (Opportunity measured by ineffective monitoring), and X6 (Collusion measured using cooperation with the government) had no effect on financial statement fraud. These findings provide important implications for stakeholders to be more aware of indicators of aggressive financial targets, opportunities, rationalization, managerial capabilities, and arrogance as key signals of potential financial report manipulation in the infrastructure sector.

title: Human rights allegations in supply chains: the impact of reverberation on financial markets and social evaluations
summary: Purpose This study examines the relationship between the reverberation of follow-up news of a firm's human rights allegations concerning working conditions on share price volatility and social score. These allegations may generate reputational risks that are amplified by NGO and media coverage, thereby shaping financial and social analysts' evaluations of the firm's ability to manage such risks. We also test whether the adoption of human rights policies moderates these potential negative effects. Design/methodology/approach To test our hypotheses, we constructed a firm-year panel comprising 147 US-based firms from 2015 to 2022. We combined data on human rights allegations against firms and their follow-up news from the Business and Human Rights Research Center, sustainability information from the Bloomberg ESG module, financial data from Compustat and stock market data from the CRSP database. Findings Our results show that follow-up news reverberation of a firm's human rights allegations is associated with reduced share price volatility, as sustained information may make a firm's actions more visible and predictable to shareholders. Conversely, this reverberation negatively affects a firm's social score, especially in the case of negative follow-up news and in the presence of human rights policies. Reverberation may reveal a decoupling between a firm's stated commitments and its actual behavior regarding human rights. Originality/value This paper reframes human rights allegations as reputational and human rights risks perceived by investors and social evaluators, who respond differently based on the reverberation of such allegations as amplified by NGOs and the media.

title: Market capitalization as a stability challenge in the capital market: Evidence from Nepalese banking sector
summary: Traditional finance views stock market and portfolio choices as products, brand, market efficiency, investors' behavior, and rationality. However, research suggests that different factors affect the share market capitalization for its stability. The strategy's role of investment, innovation, SMEs, and financial sustainability has become more crucial for Nepalese economies driven by the interaction among the investors, financial markets, venture capital ecosystem, and sustainable finance. This exploratory study aims to examine the status of market capitalization and its financial determinants, explore the relationship between market capitalization and financial indicators, and analyze the impact of earnings per share (EPS), dividend payout ratio (DPR), return on equity (ROE), book value per share (BVPS), interest rates (IRs), and number of outstanding shares (NOSs) on market capitalization. The study employs a descriptive and causal-comparative research design, utilizing purposive sampling to select 10 commercial banks. The secondary data are acquired from the report of Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB) and the annual report of the respective bank. The data is analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and regression analysis. The study's findings reveal a positive relationship between book value per share, outstanding shares, and market capitalization. In contrast, earnings per share, dividend payout ratio, return on equity, and interest rate do not significantly impact market capitalization. Thus, book value per share and outstanding shares are significant variables affecting market capitalization. The study concludes that structural financial indicators like book value per share and the number of shares are of greater importance in determining the market capitalization of Nepalese commercial banks than profitability and macroeconomic indicators. The study recommends that stakeholders in the Nepalese banking sector, including policymakers and management, adopt enhanced financial sustainability frameworks and regulatory support to foster sustainable growth and attract investors.

title: The impact of environmental uncertainty and managerial myopia on corporate ESG performance
summary: Using panel data on Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2022, this study examines the effects of environmental uncertainty and managerial myopia on corporate ESG performance and further investigates the moderating role of bank credit support. The findings show that both environmental uncertainty and managerial myopia have significant negative effects on corporate ESG performance. Moreover, bank credit support mitigates the adverse effects of environmental uncertainty and managerial myopia on corporate ESG performance. Heterogeneity analyses indicate that these negative effects are more pronounced among non-state-owned enterprises and firms in high-technology industries. By integrating environmental uncertainty and managerial short-term orientation, this study provides a unified framework for understanding how external operating conditions and managerial decision horizons jointly shape corporate ESG performance. It also highlights bank credit as a potential buffer against both external and internal short-term pressures. The findings have practical implications for promoting corporate sustainability and strengthening corporate governance.

title: Corporate Corruption and Patriarchal Power: A Feminist Critique of Governance and Accountability
summary: This article develops a critical feminist account of corporate corruption, challenging conventional approaches that treat corruption as individual misconduct within otherwise legitimate governance systems. It argues instead that corruption is structurally enabled by Western corporate governance itself: particularly contractarian ideology, shareholder primacy, and legal frameworks that privilege capital while externalising social and environmental harms. Through comparative analysis of Australia, Canada, and the United Kingdom, the article demonstrates how formally permissive approaches to stakeholder interests leave shareholder-oriented norms largely intact and obscure the gendered, racialised, colonial, and ecological consequences of corporate power. Adopting an intersectional feminist lens, it reconceptualises corruption beyond bribery and financial exchange to encompass abuses of entrusted power and systemic forms of extraction, including sextortion and legally sanctioned practices that disproportionately harm Indigenous communities, racialised women, workers, and women in the Global South. The article rejects representational and voluntary reforms to corporate social responsibility and environmental, social and governance frameworks as insufficient, arguing instead for structural governance redesign. It advances binding fiduciary obligations, participatory and Indigenous-informed governance, stronger enforcement institutions, and intersectional accountability as necessary to redistribute corporate power and reorient corporate governance toward substantive equality, democratic accountability, and equitable and sustainable stewardship.

summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis proses pemberdayaan petani kopi melalui pemanfaatan program Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) di Desa Cibeusi, Kecamatan Ciater, Kabupaten Subang. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode studi kasus untuk memperoleh pemahaman yang mendalam mengenai proses pemberdayaan yang berlangsung pada kelompok tani penerima program CSR. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara mendalam, observasi, dan studi dokumentasi, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan teknik analisis data interaktif melalui reduksi data, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan perspektif Green Social Work sebagai kerangka utama untuk memahami dimensi sosial dan ekologis, serta Creating Shared Value sebagai perspektif pendukung dalam menjelaskan penciptaan nilai bersama antara perusahaan dan masyarakat. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa program CSR telah berkontribusi terhadap peningkatan kapasitas petani melalui pelatihan budidaya, pendampingan, penguatan kelembagaan kelompok tani, pengembangan praktik agroforestri, serta peningkatan akses pasar. Program tersebut juga mendorong meningkatnya partisipasi masyarakat, kesadaran ekologis, dan keberlanjutan usaha tani kopi. Dari perspektif Creating Shared Value, kemitraan antara perusahaan dan kelompok tani menghasilkan manfaat timbal balik berupa peningkatan kualitas produksi, keberlanjutan rantai pasok, dan penguatan hubungan sosial antara perusahaan dengan masyarakat. Penelitian ini menawarkan model pemberdayaan petani kopi berbasis CSR yang mengintegrasikan dimensi sosial, ekonomi, dan lingkungan sebagai kontribusi konseptual bagi pengembangan program pemberdayaan masyarakat berkelanjutan.

title: Problems of qualification of nazi propaganda in conditions of digital transformation
summary: Problem. In the context of digital transformation, extremist ideology, including Nazism, has acquired new forms of dissemination in information and telecommunication networks, which has significantly complicated the qualification of crimes related to Nazi propaganda. Aim. To identify and analyze the problems of qualification of crimes provided for in Articles 280, 282, 282.4 and 354.1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation, committed using information and telecommunication networks, and to propose criteria for their differentiation based on the dominant purpose of the act, as well as to formulate recommendations for improving law enforcement practice, taking into account modern forms of digital propaganda. Methods. The research material was based on the norms of the Russian criminal legislation (Articles 280, 282, 282.4, and 354.1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation), resolutions of the Plenum of the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation, and case materials on Nazi propaganda in information and telecommunication networks for the period 2024–2025. The primary method employed was formal legal analysis, which allowed identifying common and distinguishing features of the elements of crimes. Results. Based on the analysis of Articles 280, 282, 282.4, and 354.1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation and judicial practice materials for 2024–2025, the following issues were identified: problems of composition competition, determining the moment of crime commission in information and telecommunication networks, and distinguishing between public and private communication. The research proposed qualification criteria based on the dominant purpose of the act: rehabilitation of Nazi ideology (Article 354.1), inciting hostility using Nazi rhetoric as a tool (Article 282), and cumulative qualification in cases of two independent intentions. The study substantiated the need to expand the concept of Nazi propaganda to include modern digital forms such as meme culture, trolling, and automated systems. Conclusions. The current criminal legislation does not fully take into account the specifics of the digital environment, which generates legal conflicts in the qualification of Nazi propaganda in information and telecommunication networks. The key role in overcoming these conflicts belongs to the Plenum of the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation, which should provide clarifications on the issues of intent assessment and content orientation, as well as develop criteria for distinguishing public actions from private communication in the digital space.

title: TRANSFORMATION OF ELECTRONIC BUSINESS IN DIGITAL ECONOMY
summary: One of the most significant changes that is happening today is the transition to an information society based on knowledge that intensively uses the Internet and other information and communication technologies in the execution of economic, business and daily life activities. The digital economy, as the main segment of this society, is characterized by the digitization of many products and services, as well as the use of the Internet and other networks in the execution of economic activities. Traditional markets are transforming into digital markets where fierce competition takes place in dynamic conditions, with rapid and major changes. This all led to changes in the way of conducting business, and especially in the way of managing business transactions with the company's trading partners. Electronic business and commerce (e-commerce) implies that every transaction takes place over the Internet and other networks, such as wireless mobile networks. title: Managing value of decommissioning obligations in mining industry – key challenging issues from the financial reporting perspective
summary: This article presents the evolution of financial reporting regulations and practices regarding decommissioning liabilities with a focus on the managerial approach to value creation processes in mining companies. Firstly, the author demonstrates the importance of provisions for the above-mentioned obligations for their overall financial standings. Than an analyses of the US and European financial reporting regulations from 1999 up to recent developments is provided to identify two fundamental challenges, related to: (a) a discount rate that should be applied to actualize cash flows needed to settle decommissioning liabilities, or broader, to proper inclusion of the risk factor into computations, (b) value recognition of post-retirement assets or broader, efficient management of these assets to maximize a mining project and company value. It has been proved that discounting is not a proper technique to deal with uncertainty of cash flows needed to settle decommissioning obligations, as mirroring a recognized practice applied for investment projects leads to results which are not only counterintuitive but significantly underestimate their current values. Therefore, a risk-free rate should be applied, and other methods must be developed to include uncertainty factors into computations. With respect to post-closure asset management, consequences of accounting treatment of gains from asset disposal have been analyzed. A need for adopting a broader perspective encompassing non-mining-related use of such assets in the ESG context was indicated. The article also demonstrates the value of mining industry experience for other industries facing similar problems, like renewable energy.

title: Development of Accounting Practices and Disclosure in the Light of the Shift towards Artificial Intelligence
summary: The purpose of this research is to contribute to the development of the accounting process and disclosure in the context of the disruption that brings in artificial intelligence by providing an integrated framework, from the perspective of internal development of accounting processes to the external requirements of the disclosure. The framework is based on the following five pillars: digital transformation policies; influence of artificial intelligence on the quality of accounting information; basic principles of intelligent models; governance mechanisms; and related risks. This is a descriptive and analytical study. It discussed the theoretical background and accounting implications of artificial intelligence, proposed a disclosure framework, and then it utilized content and gap analysis to determine to what extent the considered annual report met the requirements of the frameworkThe above analysis was based on the 2024 annual report of Asiacell Communications Company-Private Joint Stock Company. The disclosures of artificial intelligence, digital transformation, applications in accounting and finance, information quality, governance, and technological risk were selected and analyzed together with 24 disclosure items based on the proposed framework. The findings show a large disparity between the technological sophistication of the company and its level of accounting disclosure on artificial intelligence. The fermentations described in the present disclosure examples were at 25%, but only 25% of the disclosures were reached, and disclosures of assumptions underlying predictive models and related risks were missing. The results also suggest that the introduced framework, if adopted, would cover all the 24 disclosure items with a maximum proposed disclosure score of 100%.Also, based on model assumptions, data sources, levels of confidence, responsibilities in governance, and procedures for verification, transparency would be increased, the credibility of accounting estimates would be strengthened, the level of information uncertainty would be decreased, and the level of investor confidence in financial reports produced in an artificial intelligence milieu would be enhanced

title: COMPARING ESG RATING APPLICATIONS IN THE CHINESE AND KAZAKHSTANI BANKING SECTORS
summary: The purpose of the research is to contrast ESG rating practices in Chinese and Kazakhstani banking industries, representing countries at different levels of ESG institutionalization. The methodology used in the research is a multi-method qualitative and descriptive study involving comparative approach, descriptive analysis, and case study methods. The Chinese sample consists of five largest banks operating in China – ICBC, CCB, ABC, CMB, and CITIC. They were evaluated according to Huazheng ESG index during 2020-2025. For Kazakh sample, there are five banks involved – Bank CenterCredit, Jusan Bank, Otbasy Bank, Development Bank of Kazakhstan, and Halyk Bank, which were evaluated according to the external ratings offered by S&P Global CSA, Sustainable Fitch, and MSCI/Sustainalytics. Overall, there are thirteen sources analyzed, out of which twelve represent peer-reviewed articles found within the Scopus database and academic journals of the Republic of Kazakhstan. The last source represents an official normative act of Astana Financial Services Authority (AFSA). In general, China has created a full-fledged dual-system of ESG rating including domestic providers (Huazheng ESG), along with international agencies under strong regulations and regular data updating. On the other hand, the Kazakhstan banking industry is still at the beginning of its ESG evolution path. It is completely based on internationally recognized rating methodologies. There are no domestic rating systems in place; there is an immature regulatory system, and poor data availability, with the first ratings disclosed in 2022–2024 years, except for Halyk Bank that obtained its first MSCI rating in 2020. This work adds to the literature on comparative ESG studies by providing a well-developed institution-based bilateral analysis of a less studied country pair. title: The Impact of Green Finance and Cultural Preservation on Sustainable Development in Vietnam
summary: This paper evaluates the impact of Green Finance (GF) and Cultural Preservation (CP) on Sustainable Development (SD) in Vietnam, while examining the mediating role of Cultural Preservation and the moderating role of Community Awareness/Supportive Policies (MO). Utilizing a quantitative research design with a empirical survey sample of residents, enterprises, and local authorities across key heritage and ecotourism regions, the analysis was executed through a multi-stage statistical pipeline: Cronbach’s Alpha reliability analysis, Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA), and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The empirical findings reveal that both Green Finance and Cultural Preservation exert significant direct positive effects on Sustainable Development. Crucially, Cultural Preservation acts as a vital partial mediator, transforming green financial capital into sustainable economic, environmental, and social values. Based on these insights, managerial implications and policy recommendations are proposed to promote green financial mechanisms intrinsically linked to cultural heritage preservation in Vietnam.

title: SUPPLY CHAIN RISK, TRADE CREDIT PROVISION, AND THE ROLE OF LIQUIDITY PRESERVATION
summary: We document that firms exposed to greater supply chain risk extend less trade credit. This result is robust to multiple identification strategies, including an instrumental variables approach, a system GMM estimator, and a quasi-natural experiment exploiting the exogenous increase in supply chain risk during the global financial crisis. Subsample analyses show that the effect is stronger among firms facing heightened product market competition and financial constraints. Taken together, the evidence indicates that supply chain risk materially shapes firms’ trade credit policies. Our findings also offer practical implications for frontier markets such as Vietnam, suggesting that firms may respond to heightened supply chain risk by preserving liquidity through more conservative trade credit policies.

title: Environmental, Social, and Governance Information Disclosure: Who Discloses Wins?
summary: ABSTRACT As Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Information Disclosure (ESG‐ID) transitions from voluntary to mandatory disclosure, its drivers and impacts have become focal points of discussion. Existing research, however, lacks integration, which, in turn, has led to fragmented theoretical and practical insights. This study conducts a multi‐layered systematic literature review on ESG‐ID following the Scientific Procedures and Rationales for Systematic Literature Reviews (SPAR‐4‐SLR) protocol. At Layer 1, a broad bibliometric analysis is performed on 1507 articles retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science to delineate the field's developmental trajectory. At Layer 2, a TCCM‐ADO‐based content analysis is applied to 437 articles published in ABDC A*/A‐ranked journals, uncovering the theoretical underpinnings (T), contextual settings (C), characteristic patterns (C), and methodological approaches (M) that inform ESG‐ID research while simultaneously examining the antecedents (A), disclosure decisions (D), and outcomes (O) of ESG‐ID. Through this review, an integrated knowledge framework was established to serve as a reference point for the theoretical advancement and practical application of ESG‐ID. Notably, the framework posits that firms' ESG disclosure choices regarding strategy, form, and quality are driven and impeded by internal and external antecedents . These choices translate into economic, informational, and relational outcomes through specific transmission mechanisms. Key mediators include analyst attention, corporate culture, financing constraints, green innovation, information transparency, and profit sustainability. Disclosure effectiveness may be conditioned by key moderators such as ownership structure, digital transformation, industry exposure, and public attention. However, the positive impact of ESG‐ID is not universal, as such disclosure may lose its effectiveness or even lead to negative consequences when assurance is insufficient or greenwashing is detected.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Gender Equality as Drivers of the Economic Efficiency of Kazakhstan's Digital Transformation
summary: The article examines artificial intelligence as a tool for modernizing public administration and as a potential factor in the economic efficiency of digital transformation. The study aims to develop and substantiate a conceptual-analytical framework identifying channels through which gender-sensitive AI in Kazakhstan’s public sector may be associated with transaction costs, budget targeting, labor-force participation, and returns to human capital, and to specify indicators for subsequent empirical assessment. The methodology combines institutional economic analysis, a comparative approach, policy analysis, elements of gender impact assessment, and logical modelling. The empirical and documentary basis includes official Kazakhstan data on e-government and the labor market, the Law “On Artificial Intelligence,” the Concept for the Development of Artificial Intelligence for 2024–2029, Bureau of National Statistics data, ILOSTAT, ITU DataHub, Women, Business and the Law, and OECD, UNESCO, and UN Women publications. The analysis identifies potential economic channels rather than statistically established causal effects. The scientific novelty is an economic-institutional extension of Algorithmic Accountability, Algorithmic Fairness, Responsible AI, and gender-responsive AI through the concept of gender-algorithmic accountability, which links gender-differentiated AI outcomes with transaction costs, budget targeting, employment, human capital, and returns on public digital investment. Practical implications concern gender auditing of high-risk AI systems, gender- and region-disaggregated monitoring of digital services, fairness requirements in public procurement, and support for women’s economic participation.

title: Absolute Sustainability by Design: From Molecules to Processes, Supply Chains, and Planetary Boundaries
summary: Chemists want to design molecules and catalysts that are environmentally sustainable. But whether a new molecule is sustainable does not depend on its structure and reaction alone. It depends on the system built around it: the reactor and separation steps used at scale, the utilities supplying them such as electricity and high-temperature heat, the supply chains delivering feedstocks and products, and how all of this fits into a pathway towards a future net-zero circular economy that stays within the safe operating space of the planet. We present the vision of an integrated toolchain that spans these scales, from molecular design to planetary boundaries. The toolchain combines four pillars: (i) computer-aided molecular and process design [1] to identify promising candidate molecules and their most efficient industrial synthesis routes, (ii) time-explicit life cycle assessment [2] to evaluate environmental impacts dynamically by accounting for evolving future production systems, (iii) transition pathway optimization [3] for strategic deployment planning and the design of robust, long-term supply chain networks, and (iv) absolute sustainability assessment [4], which evaluates system-wide environmental impacts against the planetary boundary framework to ensure future pathways do not transgress ecological limits. By equipping chemists with an accessible yet comprehensive framework, this toolchain bridges the gap between molecular design and systems engineering. Researchers can anticipate the macro-level consequences of micro-level design choices early in development, avoiding regrettable substitutions where a molecule appears sustainable in the lab but creates severe environmental bottlenecks at industrial scale. title: The Implementation of Smart Farming and Integrated Supply Chains to Ensure Food Security and Price Stability in East Java
summary: Objective: This study aims to analyze the implementation of Smart Farming and supply chain integration as strategies to ensure food security and price stability in East Java. Design/Methods/Approach: This study used a descriptive qualitative document-analysis design. The study purposively selected government policy documents, official publications, program reports, and peer-reviewed articles, then analyzed them using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase thematic analysis—coding combined deductive categories derived from the research objectives with inductive codes emerging from the documents. Source triangulation, a document-extraction matrix, an audit trail, and repeated theme review strengthened analytical trustworthiness. Findings: The research findings indicate that the implementation of Smart Farming, including soil moisture monitoring, crop growth sensors, and data-driven weather forecasting, contributes to increased productivity and reduced crop losses. Supply chain integration through digital platforms and cooperative collaboration has also been shown to support more efficient distribution and help mitigate price fluctuations. Originality/Value: This study provides insights into how Smart Farming technology and supply chain integration can contribute to food security and price stability in East Java, addressing both agricultural efficiency and market stability. Practical/Policy implication: This study recommends strengthening technology adoption, policy support, and supply chain partnerships as strategic steps towards sustainable food security in East Java.

title: Supply Chain Network-Based Path Optimization for Customized Product
summary: The increasing demand for customized products has significantly increased the complexity of supply chain operations, making efficient path planning an important issue for reducing overall supply chain costs. This study proposes a supply chain network (SCN)-based path optimization model for customized product supply chains. The proposed model simultaneously optimizes node selection and transportation routes while minimizing transportation, processing, and fixed operating costs. To solve the optimization problem, a Genetic Algorithm (GA) with integer encoding is employed. Numerical experiments are conducted under different supply chain network scales to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed model. The experimental results indicate that the proposed approach can effectively identify cost-efficient node configurations and transportation routes while maintaining stable convergence across different network scales. The proposed model provides an effective optimization framework for customized product supply chain design and offers useful managerial implications for supply chain network planning and cost management.

title: Review of digital transformation of public services in Kazakhstan
summary: The article reviews the new stage of digital transformation of public services in Kazakhstan in 2025-2026. The empirical base includes full-year 2025 statistics on online and mobile public services, public monitoring of service quality, and results of the digital modernization of the civil service. The regulatory analysis covers the 2025 Law on Artificial Intelligence, the 2026 Digital Code of the Republic of Kazakhstan, the new 2026 Law on Civil Service, the updated legal regime for public and socially responsible services, and the renewed institutional mandate of the Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development. In 2025, citizens received more than 51.5 million public services online; eGov Mobile had more than 11.7 million users, while the average public-monitoring score for service quality reached 4.88 out of 5. Current official 2026 reporting indicates that 92% of public services are available online and that the share obtained via smartphones has reached 95.9%. The available evidence primarily indicates wider access, changing service channels, and stronger proactive control; however, open statistics are insufficient to conclude that budget expenditure has declined or civil-service productivity has increased. At the same time, digital inequality, data interoperability, cybersecurity, and algorithmic transparency remain significant constraints.

title: Digital transformation of professional training in the prison system
summary: The article examines the strategic priorities of state policy and the main technological trends in the digitalization of vocational education in the penitentiary system of the Russian Federation. The results of empirical studies confirm a high adaptive potential but highlight the need for specialized secure platforms under the conditions of regime restrictions. The necessity of developing departmental advanced training programs, a motivation system, and a shift towards qualitative performance indicators is substantiated. Measures are proposed to establish ethical and legal norms for the use of AI, aimed at balancing technological sovereignty with the preservation of the fundamental nature of staff training.

title: Global Supply Chains and Policy Shocks: Implications for Sectoral Wages
summary: ABSTRACT This paper investigates the heterogeneous transmission of global supply chain disruptions, trade policy uncertainty, tariffs and monetary policy shocks to United States sectoral wages from March 2007 to June 2025. Estimating a Bayesian structural vector autoregression model for major economic sectors, we quantify the dynamic wage responses and calculate the forecast error variance decompositions to identify the primary drivers of wage volatility. The empirical estimates document substantial sectoral heterogeneity. Global supply chain disruptions create significant inflationary pressures on wages, heavily concentrated within service and logistics industries. In contrast, trade policy uncertainty acts as a broad deflationary force across the labour market. Tariff implementations generate sharply divided outcomes between protected and exposed sectors. Additionally, contractionary monetary policy has its most severe dampening effects on wages in interest‐rate‐sensitive, goods‐producing industries. By jointly evaluating these structural shocks at a detailed level, this study demonstrates that aggregate macroeconomic analyses hide critical labour market dynamics, providing highly specific estimates of the distinct forces dictating sectoral wage growth.

title: Sustainability and reverse supply chain, the mediating role of ecological innovation
summary: The mounting obstacles of waste management and the increasing importance of ecological innovation, reverse supply chains become apparent tactic by organizations for resource retrieval, value creation, and reducing environmental footprint .This study examines the influence of sustainable practices such as sustainable procurement, green supplier collaboration, management commitment and environmental regulations on reverse supply chain with the mediation of ecological innovation in Iraqi small and medium enterprises. The study adopted a quantitative design and the data were collected from 350 questionnaire survey sent to owners and managers of manufacturing firms in Iraq. The author employed (PLS-SEM) to analyze the relationship among variables. The results show sustainable procurement, green supplier collaboration, top management commitment positively impacted ecological innovation. In contrast, environmental regulations have no direct effect on ecological innovation. This outcome can be explained by weak enforcement of environmental regulations in Iraq. In addition, ecological innovation mediates the relation between procurement, green supplier collaboration, top management commitment and reverse supply chain. This study exposes how ecological innovation acts as the internal bridge that transforms general sustainability practices into concrete, efficient reverse supply chain operations, addressing a key gap in manufacturing and logistics research.

summary: Digital transformation has become a critical strategic path for enterprises to enhance performance. Studies show that the in-depth application of digital technologies can significantly reduce transaction costs, accelerate market response, and expand the boundaries of value creation. However, transformation outcomes are moderated by contextual factors including firm size, industry characteristics, and institutional environment. Notably, successful digital transformation requires the synergistic evolution of technology application, organizational change, and strategic innovation, rather than simple technological superposition. This paper not only reveals the complex relationship between digital transformation and firm performance but also provides a theoretical basis for enterprises to formulate differentiated transformation strategies.

title: Systematic bias in Scope 3 emissions accounting: evidence from firm-level supply networks
summary: Scope 3 emissions often constitute the largest share of corporate greenhouse gas footprints, yet their accounting remains highly sensitive to incomplete supplier-level information and the replacement of aggregated emission-intensity proxies. Here, using Toyota Motor Corporation as a firm-level case study, we examine the data gap of third-party supply-chain databases and assess how the granularity and source of emission-intensity data shape upstream Scope 3 estimates. We construct a five-tier supply-chain network for this company, drawing upon publicly available supplier-customer relationships, firm financial reports, geographic information and a gravity model used for trade volumes prediction, which is therefore conservative, transparent, and reproducible for shareholders to implement and verify. Benchmark with the network constant, four emission-intensity scenarios, ranging from firm-level intensities to subindustry-, sector-, and MRIO-based sector averages are compared. Results show that sector-average emission intensities would overestimate the Scope 3 emissions; the magnitude of the overestimates hinges on the data scales and database selections. This study further reveals a pronounced emissions concentration, with the first-tier suppliers accounting for around 60% of upstream embodied emissions across the five supply tiers. A similar emissions concentration also exists among a small number of carbon-intensive suppliers within each supply tier; most of them are engaged in raw materials provision and energy-intensive activities. Firm-level analysis of emission hotspots also demonstrates that trade network reconstruction can improve the interpretability and decision relevance of corporate Scope 3 accounting by revealing where embodied emissions are concentrated and how mitigation efforts can be prioritized across global supply networks.

title: EXTERNAL ASSURANCE QUALITY AND THE VALUATION OF SUSTAINABILITY PERFORMANCE
summary: This research investigates the effect of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance on firm value by considering the quality of external assurance in the Indonesian capital market. Using a quantitative approach, the study analyzes 87 firm-year observations of publicly listed companies with available ESG data and sustainability reports during 2022–2024. The hypotheses are tested using panel data regression and moderated regression analysis. The robustness tests are also performed using alternative proxies for firm value. The results reveal that ESG performance significantly enhances a company’s market valuation. Furthermore, the quality of external assurance fails to moderate the positive effect of ESG performance on a firm's market valuation. This study extends the existing literature by examining the quality of external assurance as a moderating variable in the relationship between ESG performance and firm value in the Indonesian capital market, where empirical evidence remains limited. This research enriches the current literature by providing empirical evidence that ESG performance functions as a critical signaling mechanism for investors when assessing a company's prospects and sustainability. The findings encourage companies to improve ESG performance, regulators to standardize external assurance, and investors to incorporate ESG into investment decisions.

title: Effect of Digital Transformation on Smart Business Model Adoption in Retail Firms: Evidence from fsQCA
summary: As smart business model innovation has become a strategic priority for retail companies looking to improve their competitiveness, digital transformation has emerged as a strategic imperative. But the research to date generally only considers the individual impacts of digital transformation capabilities, with linear analytical approaches, offering limited knowledge about the interactions of capabilities in the adoption of smart business models. This study aims to fill this gap by exploring the configurational pathway to the adoption of smart business models within retail companies in China. The study is based on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) Framework that considers the roles of digital leadership, digital technology capability, organizational agility, digital skills, and customer digital orientation. A structured questionnaire with five-point Likert-scale measures was used to collect data from 130 managers from Chinese retail companies. The data were analysed using Fuzzy-set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA), which was used to draw out the necessary and sufficient conditions and configurations for high smart business model adoption. The findings show that the necessary condition for smart business model adoption is capability with digital technology. In addition, three other types of digital transformation capabilities are found, showing that smart business models can be adopted on multiple strategic paths within retail. The findings also validate the concepts of equifinality and causal asymmetry which means that the configurations that contribute to successful adoption of a business model are different from those that contribute to unsuccessful adoption. It makes a contribution to the literature on digital transformation and business model innovation by using a configurational approach to capability integration and it expands the use of fsQCA in the research on digital transformation. The results also provide valuable recommendations for retail managers and policy makers looking to push digital transformation faster and to create smart and sustainable business models in an ever-competitive digital economy.

title: Barriers to the Adoption of Industry 4.0 Technologies in the Digital Agri-Food Supply Chain
summary: Food waste in the agricultural sector remains a critical challenge with far-reaching impacts for food security and resource efficiency. In response, digitalization has increasingly been integrated into the Agri-Food Supply Chain (AFSC) to ease these losses. However, before effective digital solutions can be implemented, it is essential to identify and cognize the barriers within the digital AFSC. Only then can meaningful strategies be developed to overcome these obstacles. This study delineates the barriers and consequences of Industry 4.0 technologies in the AFSC through an analysis of current literature and expert perspectives. A total of 18 barriers were identified across the technical, operational, organizational and strategic dimensions. We use both the Matrix of Cross-Impact-Multiplication Applied to a Classification (MICMAC) method and interpretive structural modelling (ISM) to model these barriers. The results suggest that security and privacy concerns, technological immaturity, lack of technological infrastructure, high initial costs, uncertainty in Return On Investment (ROI), and lack of government regulation are the most important driving barriers within the hierarchical structure. Consequently, this research focuses on constraints that have emerged in the digital AFSC. This study serves as a guide for addressing supply chain issues in the Indian agri-food sector amid high demand for agricultural products.

title: FROM LEDGERS TO ALGORITHMS: MAPPING FINTECH'S IMPACT ON FINANCE AND ACCOUNTING THROUGH BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS (1989–2025)
summary: This study examines the impact of financial technologies (FinTech), management information systems, and artificial intelligence (AI) on finance, accounting, and business processes. It explores how AI-supported FinTech applications contribute to risk management, security, customer experience, and transaction automation, while discussing their advantages and limitations. Publications indexed in the Web of Science database between 1989 and 2025 were analyzed. A total of 3,691 documents were examined using bibliometric analysis to identify publication trends, collaboration structures, and key conceptual themes. The findings reveal significant growth in FinTech research, with AI emerging as a central research theme. China and the United States lead AI integration in FinTech research. Major challenges include data privacy, cybersecurity, and algorithmic bias. Although AI improves financial services, risk management, and business processes, it cannot fully replace human judgment. The study identifies research gaps and future directions for integrating FinTech, AI, accounting information systems, and business processes.

title: Pengaruh Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) dan Leverage terhadap Kinerja Keuangan Perusahaan pada PT Astra International Tbk Periode 2016-2025
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) dan leverage terhadap kinerja keuangan PT. Astra International Tbk periode 2016-2025, baik secara parsial maupun simultan. Penelitian menggunakan metode kuantitatif dengan data sekunder berupa laporan keuangan dan laporan tahunan perusahaan selama periode penelitian, yang dianalisis menggunakan uji t untuk melihat pengaruh parsial dan uji F untuk melihat pengaruh simultan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa secara parsial CSR berpengaruh signifikan terhadap kinerja keuangan (signifikansi 0,037 < 0,05; t-hitung 2,670 > t-tabel 2,364), sedangkan leverage tidak berpengaruh signifikan (signifikansi 0,086 > 0,05; t-hitung 2,050 < t-tabel 2,364). Secara simultan, CSR dan leverage tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap kinerja keuangan (signifikansi 0,094 > 0,05; F-hitung 3,592 < F-tabel 5,14). Temuan ini mengindikasikan bahwa pengungkapan CSR lebih dominan dalam memengaruhi persepsi kinerja keuangan dibandingkan tingkat leverage perusahaan. Implikasinya, perusahaan disarankan untuk terus meningkatkan kualitas dan konsistensi pengungkapan CSR sebagai strategi peningkatan kinerja keuangan, sementara kebijakan leverage perlu dikelola secara hati-hati meski pengaruhnya belum signifikan secara statistik dalam penelitian ini.
